gen_risks.description: Delay in HM Treasury approval and budget confirmation could postpone funding availability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage Treasury early, submit detailed business case, and establish a contingency funding plan.
gen_risks.evidence: Management case: success depends on timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury.

gen_risks.description: Lower than expected pupil uptake reduces attainment benefits, weakening the benefit‑cost ratio.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement targeted outreach to parents, monitor attendance data weekly, and adjust communication strategies to boost participation.
gen_risks.evidence: Economic case: BCR relies on attainment benefits; low uptake would reduce benefits.

gen_risks.description: Complexity of the mainstream funding model may confuse schools, leading to disengagement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide clear guidance notes, webinars, and a help‑desk to explain the simplified funding rates.
gen_risks.evidence: Funding model variation by disadvantage levels was deemed complicated for mainstream schools, resulting in confusion.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient physical space in some schools could limit the ability to run breakfast clubs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy technical estate advisers to assess space and recommend reconfiguration or shared‑use arrangements.
gen_risks.evidence: Technical estate advisers to test what schools can do to mitigate any space constraints.

gen_risks.description: Schools may struggle to recruit or retain staff needed for supervised childcare.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer recruitment incentives, provide training packages, and allow flexible staffing models within funding rules.
gen_risks.evidence: Costing approach assumes typical staffing patterns; risk if schools cannot staff as assumed.

gen_risks.description: Delays in procuring additional advisers through the education and children’s social care framework.
gen_risks.mitigation: Accelerate procurement timelines, set firm contract award dates, and maintain a shortlist of pre‑qualified suppliers.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement process to increase number of advisers supporting schools through the education and children's social care framework.

gen_risks.description: The internal CRM system may not be ready by the November 2025 MVP deadline, hindering school onboarding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Allocate dedicated development resources, adopt agile milestones, and have a fallback manual onboarding process.
gen_risks.evidence: Develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum-viable product from November 2025.

gen_risks.description: Call‑centre pilot for data collection could fail, limiting programme monitoring.
gen_risks.mitigation: Run a small‑scale pilot, define clear service level agreements, and retain alternative data‑submission channels.
gen_risks.evidence: Start commercial processes to begin a call-centre pilot to support data collection.

gen_risks.description: A gap in provision may occur if NSBP schools do not transition to FBC after July 2026.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create a transition checklist, monitor NSBP school sign‑ups, and provide interim support where gaps appear.
gen_risks.evidence: All NSBP schools guaranteed a place to ensure they do not have a gap in provision after NSBP closure July 2026.

gen_risks.description: Delay in the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill could postpone the mandatory duty for schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain liaison with legislative teams, prepare interim guidance, and align funding timelines with expected enactment dates.
gen_risks.evidence: Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on schools; legislation required for programme.

gen_risks.description: Changes in government priorities or budget cuts could reduce allocated funding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Demonstrate early wins, produce regular value‑for‑money reports, and build cross‑departmental support to safeguard funding.
gen_risks.evidence: Programme success depends on timely approval and budget confirmation; changes in government priorities could affect funding.

gen_risks.description: Disruptions in food supply chains may prevent schools from meeting food standards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish multiple approved suppliers, maintain buffer stock, and set contingency menus compliant with standards.
gen_risks.evidence: Food provided must be in line with school food standards.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient parental awareness could limit attendance and undermine programme objectives.
gen_risks.mitigation: Launch a coordinated communications campaign through schools, local authorities, and community groups.
gen_risks.evidence: Evaluation will measure pupil participation and identify factors influencing attendance, including parental demand.

gen_risks.description: Area cost adjustments may be higher than projected, leading to budget overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply a sensitivity buffer in the budget and review adjustments quarterly against actual labour market data.
gen_risks.evidence: Area cost adjustment applied using national funding formula; variations could affect affordability.

gen_risks.description: Onboarding of the first cohort of ~500 schools may be delayed, pushing back the April 2026 start.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a pre‑onboarding checklist, provide early technical support, and monitor progress against a detailed timeline.
gen_risks.evidence: Cohort 1 will begin delivery in April 2026; onboarding of ~500 schools required.

gt_risks.description: Lower value for money compared to the 'do minimum' option in year 1, due to the shorter funding period available for the preferred option's new cohorts of schools.
Delivery risks around staffing and food costs for schools newly onboarded to the free breakfast clubs programme.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated through early adopter (EA) scheme insights and support funding.

gt_risks.description: Uncertainty in the labour-market benefits (parental workforce participation gains) the programme is expected to deliver.
gt_risks.mitigation: Addressed through conservative assumptions in the economic modelling.
